question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $20{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -8\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-1)}{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2-1}{4+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
20{x}_{2}=20\cdot \frac{1}{5}=4.
$$
